name: stellar_parameters
label: Stellar parameters
description: The host stars' parameters with their uncertainties.
system_prompt: Extract host-star parameters from an astronomy paper, exactly as the paper reports them.
intro: For every host star (set) in the structure plan below, extract the stellar parameters the paper reports. Give each value the star's set_label.

parameters.description: what the metallicity is measured as, e.g. '[Fe/H]' or '[M/H]'
luminosity; give the unit as printed ('L_sun' for a linear value -- the app takes the log -- or 'log(L_sun)')
projected rotational velocity v sin i

rules: Report the values THIS paper gives for each star -- its own fit, or the values it adopts and uses (then say in `note` where they come from, e.g. 'adopted from Takeda et al. 2008'). Don't fill in values from other papers that this paper only mentions in passing.
When a value is given in several places (abstract, text, table), use the table value with its uncertainties.
Asymmetric uncertainties are printed as superscript/subscript (e.g. 323.21 +0.06 -0.05): `err_plus` 0.06, `err_minus` -0.05.
A value marked '(fixed)' was fixed in the fit, not measured: give it with no uncertainties and say so in `note`.

If the paper gives two determinations of one parameter (e.g. a spectroscopic Teff and an adopted/evolutionary one), give the one the paper ADOPTS for the planet analysis and mention the other in `note`.
A luminosity given as a linear value with an uncertainty: give the value and say in `note` that its uncertainty is linear (the app can't take the log of an uncertainty exactly).

Stellar values for the star in general use sample_label ''. If a solution (a sample_label with [brackets], e.g. a joint star + planet fit) reports its OWN stellar values, give those with that sample_label.
